Professor '''Alfred Lodge''' MA (1854 – 1 December 1937), was an English [[mathematician]], author, and the first president of [[Mathematical Association|The Mathematical Association]].

Alfred Lodge was born in 1854 at [[Penkhull]], [[Staffordshire]], one of nine children to Oliver Lodge (1826–1884) and Grace, née Heath (1826–1879). His siblings included [[physicist]] [[Sir Oliver Lodge]], and historians [[Sir Richard Lodge]] and [[Eleanor Constance Lodge]]. He attended [[Queen Elizabeth's Grammar School, Horncastle|Horncastle Grammar School]], afterwards studying at [[Magdalen College, Oxford]]. In 1876 he became a fellow of [[St John's College, Oxford]], and in 1884 joined the [[Royal Indian Engineering College]] at [[Egham]], there becoming a professor of [[pure mathematics]], succeeding [[Joseph Wolstenholme]] in 1889. From 1904 until after the [[First World War]] he was a master at [[Charterhouse School]].<ref name=Nature>[https://www.nature.com/nature/journal/v141/n3561/abs/141191a0.html#top "Prof. Alfred Lodge"], Obituary, ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]''. [[Nature Publishing Group]]. Retrieved 13 April 2014</ref><ref name=SMH>[https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1301&dat=19301017&id=WPFUAAAAIBAJ&sjid=2pEDAAAAIBAJ&pg=3951,2962848 "Professor Lodge Arrives in Sidney"], ''[[Sydney Morning Herald]]'', 17 October 1930, p. 10. Retrieved 13 April 2014</ref> In 1897 Lodge became the first president of [[The Mathematical Association]] after its name change from The [[Association for the Improvement of Geometrical Teaching]].<ref>[https://www.m-a.org.uk/jsp/index.jsp?lnk=831 "Presidents of the Association"], The Mathematical Association. Retrieved 13 April 2014</ref>

Lodge was at times associated with his brother Oliver Lodge's preoccupation with [[Spiritualism (movement)|psychic phenomena]], although stating that his interest only lay where this seemed to apply to mathematics.<ref name=SMH/>

Alfred Lodge died at [[Oxford]] on 1 December 1937. He was father of two sons, Charles and Christopher.<ref name=Nature/><ref name=SMH/>

==Selected publications==
*1895 – ''Mensuration for senior students''. {{isbn|1130347621}}
*1899 – ''Matter, Ether and Motion: The Factors and Relations of Physical Science'', edited English edition by Professor Alfred Lodge.<ref>[[Amos Dolbear|Dolbear, Amos Emerson]]; [https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/35658866/ ''Matter, Ether and Motion: The Factors and Relations of Physical Science''], reprint CreateSpace Independent Publishing Platform (2013), {{isbn|1484047605}}. Report in ''[[The Guardian]]'', 4 October 1899, p. 16. Retrieved 13 April 2014</ref>
*1904 – ''Elementary mechanics including hydrostatics and pneumatics'', with Oliver Lodge and Charles S. Lodge. {{isbn|1176576577}}
*1905 – ''Differential Calculus for Beginners''. {{isbn|1147272581}}
*1905 – ''Integral calculus for beginners''. {{isbn|1231963778}}
*1906 – "Semi-convergent Series for JnX" in ''Report of the [[British Science Association|British Association for the Advancement of Science]]'', 76th. Annual Meeting, York
*1910 – "Reports on the State of Science" committee report on ''The Further tabulation of [[Bessel function|Bessel Functions]]'', for the [[British Association for the Advancement of Science]], 80th Annual Meeting, Sheffield<ref>[https://archive.org/stream/reportofbritisha11scie#page/n185/mode/2up ''The Further tabulation of Bessel Functions''], in the ''State of Science report'' p. 37, [[John Murray (publishing house)|John Murray]], London, 1911, for the British Association for the Advancement of Science, 80th Annual Meeting, Sheffield, 1910. Retrieved 13 April 2014</ref>
*1923 – ''Differential Calculus for Beginners – Primary Source Edition''. {{isbn|1293005665}}
*1927 – "The Graphic Solution of Quadratic Equations", ''[[The Mathematical Gazette]]''<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3604585 | jstor=3604585 | doi=10.2307/3604585 | title=The Graphic Solution of Quadratic Equations | last1=Lodge | first1=Alfred | journal=The Mathematical Gazette | date=1927 | volume=13 | issue=187 | pages=313–318 | url-access=subscription }}</ref>
*1933 – paper on the "[[Lorentz transformation|Larmor-Lorentz transformations]]", published in the ''[[Philosophical Magazine]]''; co-written Oliver Lodge<ref>Rowlands, Peter Lodge; ''Oliver Lodge and the Liverpool Physical Society'', [[Liverpool University Press]] (1990), p. 282. {{isbn|0853230277}}</ref>
